## Summary

One-line filter on `_compute_membership` output: `netuids = sorted(int(k) for k in validity_map.keys() if int(k))`, skipping falsy int keys (netuid **0**). **Measured** intent aligns with `load_membership_receipt` / `membership_scoring_expected`, which already treat `int(n) > 0` as the scoring/API surface and expose `root_netuid_in_membership` telemetry.

## Findings

### P2 — Built membership can omit 0 while `_shrink_allowed` forbids dropping it (MODIFY)

**Measured** (`internal/subnet_universe.py`):
- `ROOT_NETUID = 0`; when `observed_members` is non-empty, `candidates.add(ROOT_NETUID)` and netuid 0 can remain in `validity_map` under key `"0"`.
- `_eligible_for_removal` returns **False** for `netuid == ROOT_NETUID` always.
- `_shrink_allowed` requires drop evidence for every netuid in `set(prior.netuids) - set(build.snapshot.netuids)`.
- `refresh_once` replaces the build with `_hold_prior(...)` when shrink is not allowed.

**Inferred**: Before this diff, `netuids` was derived from all `validity_map` keys, so a persisted LKG that included **0** in `netuids` stayed self-consistent across refreshes. After this diff, the built snapshot **always** omits 0 from `netuids` while `validity_map` may still contain `"0"`. Any prior snapshot whose `netuids` tuple still contains 0 triggers a shrink check that **cannot** succeed for that removal (root is never eligible). **Inferred**: Minor; use a walrus/comprehension helper if touched again.

3. When a verdict is parsed, the pinned record uses **`headSha: simibotHead` from the marker only**. The first-line SHA (if any) is **not** read for pinning and **not** compared to the marker.

So a SimiBot comment that parses as `PASS` is counted at the marker’s full SHA, regardless of a different SHA in the `PASS` tail.

## Summary

The move from a withdrawal regex to `passTailAllowed` is the right shape: fail-closed allowlist, caveats like `PASS, not approved` no longer parse (**measured** on the parser logic in `verdicts.ts`). SimiBot MC handling via `simibotMcHead` and `<!-- mc-verdict:<sha> -->` is wired before the subnet-review-gate marker path (**measured**).

## Finding (P2)

**`SHA_WORD` still accepts 7–11 hex “words” as tail pointers**, which conflicts with the pinned pointer rule and with the same file’s claim logic.

In `passTailAllowed`, tail SHAs are validated with:

`const SHA_WORD = /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i;`

So these tails still **parse as PASS** (**inferred** from the function, not executed here):

| Example tail | Why it should not count as a pointer | Current parser |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deadbeef` | 8 hex letters, English word, not a 40-char SHA or ≥12 prefix | **Accepted** as bare SHA word |
| `effaced` | 7 hex letters, same class | **Accepted** |
| `abcdef12345` | 11-char prefix (<12) | **Accepted** |
| `head abcdef1` | 7-char fragment after `head` | **Accepted** |

The file already documents the 12-character floor for abbreviated *claims* in `shaClaimedByComment` (“Twelve, not GitHub’s seven…”) (**measured**). Tail validation should match: **40-char full SHA, or 12–39 hex only**—not GitHub’s 7-character short form and not hex-looking English words in the 7–11 range.

That is exactly the class of “word after PASS that is not a pointer” this PR is meant to reject.

**Suggested fix:** Split tail SHA validation from claim patterns—e.g. accept only `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` or `^[0-9a-f]{12,39}$` (case as you prefer), and add unit cases for `deadbeef`, `effaced`, 11-char prefixes, and `deadbeef/effaced` if you normalize `/` in the tail. ## JWT pattern budget (head `3395325122ef0bac8e49f82c08606f706ff48444`)

Changed pattern (from diff):
`/(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,2048}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,2048}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,2048}\b/g`

Entry point: `redactSecrets` applies each `VALUE_PATTERNS` entry via `String.replace` (same as before); only this JWT row changed.

### Adversarial input: `eyJ-` × 50,000 (200,000 characters, no dots)

**inferred** — On `S = ("eyJ-")^50000`, only index `0` satisfies `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])eyJ`. Every later `eyJ` is preceded by `-`, which is in `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, so the lookbehind rejects those starts (unlike the old `\beyJ…`, which retried at each word boundary every four bytes).

At index `0`, the first segment is `{8,2048}` (not `{8,}`), so the engine backtracks at most ~2041 segment lengths before giving up on the missing `.`; that work is **constant**, not proportional to `|S|`.

The remainder of the pass is a left-to-right scan with no nested re-scans of the tail per `eyJ` start → **inferred** overall **O(n)** work on this input.

Base pattern (for contrast, **measured** only via fixture text): `\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\…` — **inferred** **O(n²)** on the same input (comment in diff matches mechanism: each `eyJ` start can greedily consume the unbounded run and backtrack on the missing dots).

### Budget (1): time at `2N` ≤ 3× time at `N`

**inferred** — When `|S|` doubles, the dominant term is the linear scan (~2×). The fixed backtrack cap at the sole anchor does not double with `n`. Expected ratio **~2×**, below the **3×** ceiling.

**measured** — Not collected in this MC session (no code runner; `compare_suite_runs` returned `eval-no-runner`).

### Budget (2): 200,000 characters ≤ 50 ms

Review scope: JWT `VALUE_PATTERNS` entry in `review-gate-bot/bot/lib/redact.ts`, plus adjacent assignment-scrub refactor in the same diff.

### JWT pattern change (**measured** from diff / **inferred** for runtime)

**Old** (base): `/\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b/g`

**New** (head): `/(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,2048}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,2048}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,2048}\b/g`

**MC could not wall-clock the pattern in this session** (**measured**: `compare_suite_runs` returned `eval-no-runner`; no execute/Node tool on the gate). The budget assessment below is **inferred** from how V8 applies the two patterns to that input, not from timers here.

#### How work grows when input length doubles

- **Old pattern — inferred:** With no dots, the first segment quantifier `{8,}` is unbounded and greedy. From each `eyJ` anchor the engine can consume almost the entire suffix before the required `.` fails, then backtracks one character at a time. Roughly Θ(n) failed attempts per anchor × Θ(n) anchors → **superlinear (quadratic) growth** when n doubles (time ratio often ≫ 3×). **Inferred: fails budget (1).**
- **New pattern — inferred:** Each segment is capped at 2048 code units. After `eyJ`, the first segment can only extend up to 2048 class characters before the mandatory `.` is checked; there is no dot in the input, so each anchor fails after **O(1)** bounded backtracking (≤2048), not O(n). ## Summary

The diff drops two GitHub round-trips per tag/verdict write by removing `isStale` from `postSlotOnce` and the immediate `alreadyPosted` re-read (guard 3) from `postVerdictComment`. That matches the PR title, but it leaves **tag** posts exposed to the push-during-post race the description calls out, while **verdict** posts still call `isStale` inside `run`. Comments at head still describe three guards and a pre-write re-read that the code no longer performs.

## Findings

### P2 — Stale `@cursor` / `@replit` tags after synchronize (**inferred**)

**measured:** At head, `postSlotOnce` sets `superseded = false` and never assigns true; `run` goes straight to `postComment` with `marker(slot, headSha)` (lines ~107–124 in `review-gate-bot/bot/lib/tag.ts`).

**measured:** Base had `if (await isStale(...)) { superseded = true; return; }` before `postComment` in the same function (removed in this PR).

**inferred:** If the channel read gate at `headSha` A and a push lands on B (or the PR turns draft) before `createComment`, a tag still goes out pinned to A. The slot comment on `postSlotOnce` still says that case must not post, but nothing enforces it. `tagOutcome`’s `superseded` branch is dead code.

**inferred:** Gate logic pins tags/verdicts to exact SHAs (`verdictAt`, `replitTaggedForSha === headSha` in `gate.ts`), so a stale marker may not satisfy the *new* head’s gate, but it still triggers reviewer pings for a head that is no longer current — the failure mode the removed guard documented.

### P2 — Documentation contradicts behavior (**measured**)

**measured:** Module header still says `` `postVerdictComment` re-reads immediately before posting `` (`tag.ts` ~34–37).

**measured:** `postVerdictComment` block still lists **three** guards including guard 3 “re-read of the PR's comments as the last thing before the post” (~224–244); guard 3 and `lostToRecheck` handling were deleted.

**measured:** `lock.ts` ~27–28 still says callers re-read immediately before posting and names `postVerdictComment`; this PR does not touch `lock.ts`.

**measured:** `postSlotOnce` doc still defines `superseded` as head/draft drift before write; implementation no longer checks.

### P3 — Wider cross-process duplicate MC verdict window (**inferred**)

**measured:** `ranOnce` + non-CAS `claim` is documented best-effort across processes (`lock.ts`). Guard 3 narrowed the window between claim and `createComment` to one comment-list read adjacent to the write; removing it is intentional cost/latency trade.

**inferred:** Two processes can still both post MC verdicts for the same head; the gate keeps the latest marker at that SHA. Same verdict twice is noisy; two different tokens let the later comment win — already acknowledged in the stale doc block. Acceptable only if comments are updated to say guard 3 is gone.

## What would unblock PASS

1. Either restore `isStale` (or equivalent single PR-head read) immediately before tag `createComment`, **or** update `postSlotOnce` / `tagOutcome` docs and callers to state that tag posts may target a superseded head when synchronize wins the race.
2. Align all comments (`tag.ts` module header, `postVerdictComment`, `postSlotOnce`, `lock.ts`) with the two-guard implementation, or restore guard 3.
3. Optional: drop dead `superseded` plumbing in `postSlotOnce` if stale tags are an accepted trade.

## Head `7b1b568539ffbaaf49ccc7a4d14ff1bcceff79c5`

### Diff (measured)
When `not probe_complete and netuid not in probe_map`, `probe_val` becomes `False` instead of `None` (`internal/subnet_universe.py`).

### Pinned contract vs this change
**(2) Failed / timed-out chain read:** nothing observed; last-good membership **and validity** retained; **no deregistration clock**.

On a total probe failure, `_default_probe_fetch` returns `{}` and `probe_complete=False` (**measured** in file at head). Every prior member is in `candidates` but absent from `probe_map`, so the new line sets **`probe_val = False` for each** (**inferred** from `_compute_membership`).

That feeds `_merge_sources`’s chain-wins branch (`probe_positive is False and tmc_positive is not False`), which sets `validity="negative"` and stamps `negative_since` when absent (**measured**). That is a **deregistration clock on a failed read**, contradicting pinned contract (2). The prior `None` path kept prior positive/unobserved validity and did not start `negative_since` (**inferred** from the `probe_positive is None` branches in the same function).

`_eligible_for_removal` requires `evidence.probe is False` and `(now - negative_since).total_seconds() >= 172800` (**measured**). Incomplete reads now supply `probe=False`, so grace can elapse **without any successful chain observation**.

### Cycle 2 at fixed clock (changed code, chain read still failing every time)
Assume cycle 1 already ran at **T0** with the same failing probe and left member **N** in the prior snapshot with `negative_since = T0` (typical when TMC still lists N or `tmc_positive is not False`). Each cycle-2 build still has `probe_complete=False`, empty `probe_map`, and `probe_val=False` for N.

| Time | What cycle 2 does for N (**inferred** from head code) |
| --- | --- |
| **T0 + 47h59m59s** | Grace not met (`172799 < 172800`). N stays in `validity_map` and **remains in `netuids`**; still `validity=negative`, `negative_since` unchanged (T0). |
| **T0 + 48h00m00s** | Grace met (`172800 >= 172800`). N is **dropped** (`dropped[N]`), removed from `validity_map`, **shrunk out of `netuids`** even though the chain read never completed. |
| **T0 + 49h** | Same as 48h boundary if building from T0 state: N **already removed**; no successful chain read required for removal. |

Membership count may still include N through 47h59m59s because negative rows stay in `validity_map` until `_eligible_for_removal` (**measured** loop in `_compute_membership`).

### Severity
**P1 / blocking:** Treating probe failure as per-netuid `probe=False` poisons persisted `negative_since` and enables removal on grace while contract (2) requires retaining validity with **no** dereg clock when the chain read fails.
